title: Right a rover that has rolled onto its side at the edge of a drop-off
instruction: The rover has rolled onto its side on the track. Get it back on its wheels.
context: Small field robots roll over, and whoever recovers them rights them where they lie. A vehicle on its side pivots about its lower tyres as it is righted, so it lands a body-width further on: next to a drop-off (here a 5 cm step that stands for a ditch or verge, about 90 cm at the crawler's scale), tipping it where it lies sends it over, and the robot has to move it back first, or roll it the other way, without being told. Unlike TK-FKZCD5 (tipping a block in a stated direction), #1195 (using a step's edge as a pivot) and #228 (sliding a box to an edge), the tip itself is easy here; the test is foreseeing where the vehicle lands.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Track: a fixed deck (clamped to the table) of plywood on battens, 5 cm tall, 38 cm long (x 8 to 46) and 36 cm wide (y -6 to 30), its top painted earth brown as a packed-earth track (friction about 0.6). Its sides are painted rock grey; its right-hand long edge, at y -6, is the drop-off: a 5 cm vertical face with the bare table below it. A 6 cm wide strip of flat artificial-grass mat (pile 2 mm or less) is glued along the deck's left-hand edge (y 24 to 30), flush enough to count as deck surface. Rover: a 1:18 trail crawler (Traxxas TRX-4M with the Bronco body shell, decals removed, the shell painted yellow with a white roof), 26.2 cm long, 12.4 cm wide over the tyres, 11.7 cm tall, wheelbase 15.5 cm, 0.51 kg with a dummy battery of the real pack's mass, motor off with the drivetrain engaged so the wheels do not turn freely; black rubber tyres 5.6 cm across and 2.2 cm wide; black bumper bars front and rear, dark grey chassis. It lies on its left side on the track, nose pointing away from the robot (along +x), roof toward the robot's left and tyre treads toward the drop-off: the point midway between its axles is at x 24, and its tyre treads lie along y -2, 4 cm from the edge.
scoring: 0 if at any time the rover leaves the deck (its lowest point more than 1 cm below the deck top, over any of the deck's edges). Otherwise, measured at the end with the rover at rest (moving under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s for the last 20 control steps, 1 s at 20 Hz) and released (none of six points on each arm, its wrist joint, palm, both fingertips, tool point and the point between the pad tips, and no point along the arm from its shoulder joint to its palm, within 5 cm of the rover): 1.0 if it is upright (roof within 10 degrees of level) with all four tyres resting on the deck (each tyre's lowest point within 1 cm of the deck top and inside the deck's outline) and every tyre at least 2 cm from the drop-off edge; 0.5 if it is upright with all four tyres on the deck but at least one closer than 2 cm to the edge; 0.25 if it still lies on a side (its axles within 30 degrees of vertical) but its nearest point is at least 8 cm farther from the drop-off edge than at the start; otherwise 0. A full score ends the trial once it has held for 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the rover on its left side, nose away from the robot, with the midpoint between its axles at x 24 and its tyre treads 4 cm from the edge (measure from the edge). Check the table below the drop-off is clear.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The rover is one rigid body of boxes and cylinders at the crawler's published length, width, height, wheelbase and mass; its tyre size, body outline and centre of mass (4.8 cm above the ground) are estimates from photographs; its suspension is rigid and its wheels do not turn, as with the real crawler's drivetrain engaged. Friction: tyres 1.0, body 0.5, deck 0.6. The deck is a rigid slab; the grass strip is drawn on the deck surface; the real mat's pile (2 mm or less) is within the 1 cm tyre tolerance. Leaving the deck is judged from the rover's geometry (its lowest point), as from a video. No forces or damage are simulated.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left arm reached over the roof and touched the rover, which stayed on its side); demo: 1.0
